summary.en: Slide down through the old city with your guide. You stop at the Château, at the wall and at the bandstand, and at each one you learn a piece of Canada's history and then answer questions about it.
summary.fr: Glissez dans la vieille ville avec votre guide. Vous vous arrêtez au Château, au mur et au kiosque à musique, et à chaque halte vous apprenez un bout de l'histoire du Canada, puis vous répondez à des questions dessus.

text.en: That is fine. The snow will wait for us. Come back when you are ready.
text.fr: C'est correct. La neige va nous attendre. Revenez quand vous voudrez.

text.en: Mind the ice, and take your time. Each stop on this run teaches you a piece of Canada's history. Your task on the screen says what to do now.
text.fr: Attention à la glace, et prenez votre temps. Chaque halte de cette glissade vous apprend un bout de l'histoire du Canada. Votre mission à l'écran indique ce qu'il faut faire maintenant.

text.en: Canada was born on July 1, 1867. For many years that day was called Dominion Day. Today we call it Canada Day.
text.fr: Le Canada est né le 1er juillet 1867. Pendant de nombreuses années, cette journée s'appelait le « jour du Dominion ». Aujourd'hui, on l'appelle la fête du Canada.

source.quote: The Dominion of Canada was officially born on July 1, 1867. Until 1982, July 1 was celebrated as “Dominion Day” to commemorate the day that Canada became a self-governing Dominion. Today it is officially known as Canada Day.

verification.evidence: The Dominion of Canada was officially born on July 1, 1867. Until 1982, July 1 was celebrated as “Dominion Day” to commemorate the day that Canada became a self-governing Dominion. Today it is officially known as Canada Day.

text.en: You slid through the old city to the bandstand and answered every question along the way about Canada's history.
text.fr: Vous avez glissé à travers la vieille ville jusqu'au kiosque à musique et répondu à toutes les questions posées en chemin sur l'histoire du Canada.

prompt.en: Meet your guide at the top of the hill
prompt.fr: Retrouvez votre guide en haut de la côte

text.en: Bonjour! There you are. Mind the ice on the steps — this hill is steep.
text.fr: Bonjour! Vous voilà. Attention à la glace dans les marches — la côte est raide.

text.en: O Canada is our national anthem. People sang it here for the very first time, in 1880.
text.fr: Ô Canada est notre hymne national. On l'a chanté ici pour la toute première fois, en 1880.

source.quote: O Canada was proclaimed as the national anthem in 1980. It was first sung in Québec City in 1880.

verification.evidence: O Canada was proclaimed as the national anthem in 1980. It was first sung in Québec City in 1880.

text.en: In 1759, the British beat the French in a battle at Québec City, on the Plains of Abraham.
text.fr: En 1759, les Britanniques ont battu les Français lors d'une bataille à Québec, sur les plaines d'Abraham.

source.quote: In 1759, the British defeated the French in the Battle of the Plains of Abraham at Québec City

verification.evidence: In 1759, the British defeated the French in the Battle of the Plains of Abraham at Québec City

text.en: Now hold on tight! We stop three times going down, and I have something for you at each stop.
text.fr: Maintenant, tenez bon! On fait trois haltes en descendant, et j'ai quelque chose pour vous à chacune.

prompt.en: Slide down to the Château Frontenac

text.en: Look down at the river from here. Everything in this story starts with that water.
text.fr: Regardez le fleuve d'ici. Toute cette histoire commence avec cette eau.

text.en: The country's name came off this river. Jacques Cartier heard two captured guides use the Iroquoian word kanata, which means village. By the 1550s the name Canada was appearing on maps.
text.fr: Le nom du pays vient de ce fleuve. Jacques Cartier a entendu deux guides captifs employer le mot iroquoien kanata, qui veut dire village. Dès les années 1550, le nom Canada apparaissait sur les cartes.

source.quote: Cartier heard two captured guides speak the Iroquoian word kanata, meaning “village.” By the 1550s, the name of Canada began appearing on maps.

verification.evidence: EXPLORING A RIVER, NAMING CANADA Between 1534 and 1542, Jacques Cartier made three voyages across the Atlantic, claiming the land for King Francis I of France. Cartier heard two captured guides speak the Iroquoian word kanata, meaning “village.” By the 1550s, the name of Canada began appearing on maps. … Jacques Cartier was the first European to explore the St. Lawrence River and to set eyes on present-day Québec City and Montreal

prompt.en: Answer 5 questions about Canada's name and the first explorers
prompt.fr: Répondez à 5 questions sur le nom du Canada et les premiers explorateurs
Longez le mur de la ville

text.en: A wall like this was kept up by the side that won. What they did next is the part worth knowing.
text.fr: Un mur comme celui-ci a été entretenu par le camp vainqueur. Ce qu'il a fait ensuite, voilà ce qui vaut la peine d'être su.

text.en: The Quebec Act of 1774 let Catholics practise their religion and hold public office, which Britain did not allow at home. It brought back French civil law and kept British criminal law.
text.fr: L'Acte de Québec de 1774 a permis aux catholiques de pratiquer leur religion et d'occuper des charges publiques, ce que la Grande-Bretagne interdisait chez elle. Il a rétabli le droit civil français tout en gardant le droit criminel britannique.

source.quote: It allowed religious freedom for Catholics and permitted them to hold public office, a practice not then allowed in Britain. The Quebec Act restored French civil law while maintaining British criminal law.

verification.evidence: To better govern the French Roman Catholic majority, the British Parliament passed the Quebec Act of 1774. … It allowed religious freedom for Catholics and permitted them to hold public office, a practice not then allowed in Britain. The Quebec Act restored French civil law while maintaining British criminal law.

prompt.en: Answer 5 questions about what came after 1759
prompt.fr: Répondez à 5 questions sur ce qui a suivi 1759

text.en: A bandstand is where people gather in the open. Public life in this town is older than the music.
text.fr: Un kiosque à musique, c'est là où les gens se rassemblent au grand air. La vie publique de cette ville est plus ancienne que la musique.

text.en: In 1791 an act gave the colonies here their first assemblies elected by voters. The name Canada became official then, and has stayed ever since.
text.fr: En 1791, une loi a donné aux colonies d'ici leurs premières assemblées élues par les électeurs. Le nom Canada est devenu officiel à ce moment-là, et il est resté depuis.

source.quote: The Act also granted to the Canadas, for the first time, legislative assemblies elected by the people. The name Canada also became official at this time and has been used ever since.

verification.evidence: The Constitutional Act of 1791 divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (later Ontario) … The Act also granted to the Canadas, for the first time, legislative assemblies elected by the people. The name Canada also became official at this time and has been used ever since.

prompt.en: Answer 3 questions about the first elected assemblies
prompt.fr: Répondez à 3 questions sur les premières assemblées élues
